dashboard.label: Firmware check help
dashboard.description: What the firmware check does, how to read it and how to maintain its data.

div.p: This page explains the Firmware and security dashboard of the app aruba_network_insights: what it does, how to read it, and how to keep its data current. It assumes that you know Aruba (Central, AOS-10, AOS-8 Instant) but not Splunk. Terms from Splunk are explained where they appear.
The firmware check compares the software version of every access point that Aruba Central reports with two reference lists:

ol.li: Fixed versions (baseline). For each software train (for example AOS-10.8, AOS-10.7, AOS-8.13) the first version that contains the fix of an HPE security advisory. The shipped list holds the versions of advisory HPESBNW05162. An access point below the fixed version of its own train is rated Below fixed version.

Documented issues. Crash and reboot bugs that HPE lists as resolved in the AOS-10 release notes, per access point model and affected version range. An access point whose model and version fall into such a range is counted as in a documented issue range.

div.p: Both lists are plain tables with one row per fact and a link to the HPE source. Nothing is sent to HPE or anywhere else: the check runs inside your Splunk against the data that the Aruba Central add-on collected.

ul.li: Security: which access points still run a version that is affected by an advisory, and which fixed version you need per software train.
Planning upgrades: a list of the affected access points with model, site and current version, so that a maintenance window can be scoped.
Troubleshooting: if access points reboot or crash, the check shows whether HPE already documents a bug for exactly that model and version, with the bug ID and a link to the release note.
Reporting: the Executive summary shows the same numbers in its risk list, and every tile opens the detail.

div.p: It does not replace the HPE advisories and release notes. It is an indicator that points you to them (see section 7).
Open Risk > Firmware and security in the app menu.

div.p: The Site field above the tiles accepts a site name or a wildcard (* for all, Berlin* for all sites starting with Berlin).
The status of an access point is one of:

tr.td: At or above fixed version
The version is the fixed version of its train or newer.
Nothing.
Below fixed version
The version is older than the fixed version of its train.
Plan the upgrade to the version in the column Fixed in.
Not in baseline
There is no row for the software train of this access point.
Check the HPE advisory for this train and add a row (section 5).
Unknown version
The version string could not be read.
Check the version in Central. Usually a test or custom build.

div.p: Take an access point that reports the version 10.8.0.1_95221:

ol.li: The build suffix _95221 is removed. The version is 10.8.0.1.
The train is the first two numbers: 10.8.
The baseline row for the train 10.8 says min_fixed = 10.8.1.2.
10.8.0.1 is older than 10.8.1.2, so the status is Below fixed version.

div.p: An access point on 10.7.2.5 is compared with the fix of the train 10.7 (10.7.2.7), not with 10.8.1.2. This is how HPE publishes the fixes: one fixed version per train.

For documented issues the rule is: the model name starts with model_prefix, the version is at least fw_from and below fixed_in. The bug is listed for the release in which it first appeared as fixed, so for an older train check the release notes of your own train (the link is in the row).

The check reads the access point inventory that the add-on TA_hpe_aruba_central collects from the Aruba New Central API (field firmwareVersion and model). It uses the latest value per access point from the last 30 minutes. If a tile shows 0 checked access points, the Wireless input of the add-on does not deliver data: see Platform > Data health.
The reference lists are four tables (in Splunk they are called lookups):

div.blockquote: Rule: put your own rows only into the two _custom lists. Edits in the shipped lists are lost at the next app upgrade, because the upgrade installs the new version of those files.
div.p: The easiest editor is the Splunk app Lookup Editor (free, from Splunkbase: splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1724). Ask your Splunk administrator to install it once. Then these links open the lists in an editor that works like a spreadsheet (add row, edit cell, delete row, save):

tr.td: Fixed versions, yours
Issues, yours
Fixed versions, shipped (view only)
Issues, shipped (view only)

div.p: You need a role that may write to the app (admin or sc_admin).
Without Lookup Editor you can still add a row with a search. Open Search in the app menu and run:
div.pre: | makeresults | eval model_prefix="AP-635", fw_from="10.7.2.1", fixed_in="10.8.0.2", bug_id="AOS-268983", issue="Random reboot with kernel panic", source_url="https://arubanetworking.hpe.com/techdocs/central/aos10rn/aos-10-8-0-x/resolved-issues-in-aos-10-8-0-2.html" | fields - _time | outputlookup append=true aruba_known_issues_custom
div.p: Use aruba_firmware_baseline_custom with the columns scope, train, min_fixed, advisory, source_url, note for a fixed version. Use the same approach to correct a mistake: list the table with | inputlookup aruba_known_issues_custom, remove or change the row and write it back with | outputlookup (without append).
Fixed versions (aruba_firmware_baseline and aruba_firmware_baseline_custom)

div.p: One row per train. If the shipped list and your list have a row for the same train, yours wins. Use this when a newer advisory raises the fixed version of a train before the next app release does.
Documented issues (aruba_known_issues and aruba_known_issues_custom)

div.p: Versions are written with 2 to 4 numbers separated by dots, without letters and without the build number: 10.7.2.1, not 10.7.2.1_95221.

At the end of the help page in the app, the panel Check of the lists shows how many rows each list has and reports rows with a typing mistake, for example a version with letters or a link without https://. After saving a list, reload the dashboard Firmware and security: the change is effective immediately, no restart needed.
The panel Firmware that cannot be rated yet lists versions with the status Not in baseline or Unknown version. Each entry there is a reason to add a row.

ul.li: When HPE publishes a security advisory for Aruba / HPE Networking. Look up the fixed version for each train and enter it as a row in aruba_firmware_baseline_custom. The advisory names the fixed versions per product and train. Advisories are listed in the HPE Security Bulletin Library and published in machine-readable form at csaf.arubanetworking.hpe.com (the file changes.csv there lists new and updated advisories).

When you adopt a new AOS release. Read its Resolved Issues page in the AOS-10 release notes. Add a row to aruba_known_issues_custom for each crash or reboot bug of a model that you run. Skip bugs without a model name and bugs that only affect gateways or switches. For AOS-8 Instant see the AOS-8 release notes.
After an app upgrade. The shipped lists were replaced by the new version with the newest HPE data. Your own lists are unchanged. Remove rows from your lists that duplicate the new shipped rows.
Regularly, for example once a month, open the panel Firmware that cannot be rated yet.

Lookup: a table that Splunk reads when it runs a search. Here: the four lists above. The shipped ones are CSV files, your own ones are stored in the KV Store, a small database inside Splunk, so that app upgrades do not touch them.
Search: the entry Search in the app menu opens the search bar. Searches are written in a language called SPL. You only need it for the optional examples in section 5.1.
Macro: a named piece of search that the dashboards reuse. The check uses the macros aruba_fw_key, aruba_fw_baseline and aruba_fw_issues. You do not need to change them.
Dashboard: a page with tiles and tables. Clicking a tile or a row opens the detail.

The shipped issue list is a selection, not the complete release notes. It covers the crash and reboot bugs with a model name from the release notes of AOS-10.8.0.2 and AOS-10.8.1.2. Other releases and other bug types are not included. Add rows from the release notes of the releases you run. The absence of a row is not a statement that an access point is free of problems.

One fixed version per issue. The row names the release in which HPE lists the fix. Maintenance releases of older trains (for example 10.7.x) may contain the fix earlier. Open the link of the row and check the release notes of your train. If the fix is already in your version, add a row to your own list or ignore the entry.

Access points only. The advisory also covers Mobility Gateways managed by Central. Switches and gateways are listed under Switch and gateway firmware without a rating. You can add rows with another scope, but the dashboards evaluate only ap today.

End-of-Maintenance and End-of-Support versions. The HPE advisory states that software versions that reached End of Maintenance are presumed to be affected, even when they are not named in the table. The check rates such versions as Not in baseline and does not count them as a risk. Treat them as affected.
The result depends on the data. An access point is rated only if it reported in the last 30 minutes. The model name must be reported in Central.
Exceptions in advisories. The baseline holds one version per train. An exception (for example FIPS AP-5xx on AOS-8.13 need 8.13.3.2 FIPS) is stated in the column note.
HPE advisory HPESBNW05162 (fixed versions): csaf.arubanetworking.hpe.com/2026/hpe_networking_-_hpesbnw05162.txt
All Aruba advisories in machine-readable form: csaf.arubanetworking.hpe.com
HPE Security Bulletin Library: support.hpe.com/connect/s/securitybulletinlibrary
Software downloads of fixed versions: HPE Networking Support Portal
AOS-10 release notes: arubanetworking.hpe.com/techdocs/central/aos10rn, for example Resolved Issues in AOS-10.8.0.2 and Resolved Issues in AOS-10.8.1.2
AOS-8 release notes (example, referenced by the advisory): Resolved Issues in AOS 8.13.3.2
Lookup Editor app: splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1724
Add-on that collects the data: TA_hpe_aruba_central (HPE Aruba Central Add-on for Splunk)

panel.title: Fixed versions in use (yours first, shipped list below)

search.query: | inputlookup aruba_firmware_baseline_custom | eval list="yours" | append [| inputlookup aruba_firmware_baseline | eval list="shipped"] | table list scope train min_fixed advisory note | sort list scope train

panel.title: Documented issues in use (yours first, shipped list below)

search.query: | inputlookup aruba_known_issues_custom | eval list="yours" | append [| inputlookup aruba_known_issues | eval list="shipped"] | table list model_prefix fw_from fixed_in bug_id issue | sort list model_prefix bug_id

panel.title: Firmware that cannot be rated yet (access points of the last 30 minutes)

search.query: `aruba_central_index` sourcetype="aruba:central:ap" earliest=-30m | stats latest(firmwareVersion) as firmwareVersion latest(model) as model by serialNumber | eval scope="ap" | `aruba_fw_key` | `aruba_fw_baseline` | where fw_status!="At or above fixed version" AND fw_status!="Below fixed version" | stats count as APs values(model) as Models by firmwareVersion fw_train fw_status | rename firmwareVersion as Firmware, fw_train as Train, fw_status as Status | sort - APs
